title: Microgrid KV multiplex sharding for tensor/pipeline-aware cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a microgrid-oriented KV cache sharding layer that explicitly reasons about both tensor and pipeline parallel axes to reduce KV fragmentation, minimize cross-GPU fetches during continuous batching, and improve memory packing for heterogeneous multi-GPU topologies. The allocator should be topology-aware, support short-lived lease-based ownership for micro-batches, and provide adaptive hot-key replication to avoid tail latency spikes during bursty prefix traffic.
background: Current KV cache placement stripes slabs across GPUs with heuristics tuned for single-axis tiling. Under tensor+pipeline parallel mixes and continuous batching workloads we observe: 1) high cross-GPU KV fetch rate for mid-sequence tokens; 2) eviction/compaction churn when batch shape or sequence-length distribution changes; 3) uneven memory pressure on certain pipeline stages leading to conservative batch sizing and throughput loss. Customer SLOs for p95 token latency regress under mixed workloads and long-context evaluation tests show repeated NVLink/NCCL stalls during rendezvous fetches.
proposed_solution: 1) Microgrid topology: represent GPU layout as a 2D microgrid (pipeline-stage index, tensor-shard index). 2) Micro-slab allocator: break KV cache into micro-slabs (configurable base size e.g., 64KB) assigned to microgrid cells using a locality score that factors GPU memory slack, recent access heat (hotness score), and expected future prefetch windows from continuous batching. 3) Lease-based ownership: for each micro-batch, acquire short-lived leases for the micro-slabs needed to render tokens; leases allow parallel reads without global locks and enable safe local compaction. 4) Hot-key replication: adaptively replicate frequently-accessed micro-slabs to neighboring microgrid cells to avoid cross-stage fetches, with bounded replication factor and a decay policy. 5) Prefetch hints from batching scheduler: the continuous-batching planner emits lookahead token spans per batch; the microgrid prefetcher prioritizes micro-slabs accordingly. 6) Spill hierarchy: graceful spill to pinned host memory then NVMe with prioritized async prefetch. 7) Rendezvous fast-path: NCCL/RDMA gather for contiguous micro-slabs; fall back to on-demand async fetch for rare holes. 8) Background compaction: periodic compaction within each microgrid cell to reduce external fragmentation and reclaim slabs when memory pressure rises.
design_decisions: Use 2D microgrid coordinates (pipeline_stage, tensor_shard) instead of a flattened shard ID to expose locality for both axes.
Lease duration tuned to expected batch processing window (~10-50ms) to balance contention with stale ownership cost.
Replication limited to at most 2 neighboring cells by default; cluster-wide replication disabled to keep write/eviction complexity low.
Prefetch uses planner-provided lookahead; otherwise use exponential decay heat estimate for LRU-like fallback.
Spill targets: host-pinned RAM first, NVMe second; do not fallback to remote object storage at runtime.
Rendezvous uses NCCL gather where topology supports it (DGX-like or Cloud infra); add a mutex-protected fallback path for heterogeneous networks.
Expose knobs via runtime config: micro-slab size, replication factor, lease timeout, prefetch window, spill thresholds.
Ensure API compatibility: the high-level KV cache interface remains unchanged for callers; sharding is orthogonal to user-visible semantics.
Make microgrid allocation deterministic given seed+topology to simplify replay and debugging in CI tests.
Performance telemetry includes per-microgrid-cell hit-rate, cross-cell fetch rate, and lease contention counters.
implementation_plan: Spike (2d): implement deterministic microgrid allocator + in-memory micro-slab map. Owner: Marco. Link: (proto-PR TBD).
Scheduler integration (3d): extend continuous-batching planner to emit prefetch spans. Owner: Ravi.
Lease layer (3d): lightweight lease acquisition + release APIs with no global locks. Owner: Elena.
Replication logic (3d): adaptive replication controller with decay policy. Owner: Marco.
Rendezvous fast-path (4d): NCCL gather integration + fallback async path. Owner: Tobias.
Spill hierarchy + prefetch from host/NVMe (3d): async IO worker + prioritization. Owner: Ming.
Background compaction + metrics (2d): compactor and telemetry counters. Owner: Aisha.
E2E integration tests + perf harness (4d): create synthetic workloads covering long-context, bursty prefixes, and mixed tensor/pipeline parallelism. Owner: QA team.
PR reviews, security checklist, and doc updates (2d): Confluence design doc and runtime flags. Owner: Marco/Aisha.
testing_plan: Microbenchmarks: per-token latency and p95 under synthetic continuous batching with variable lookahead (0,1,3,10 tokens).
Scale tests: run on heterogeneous cluster shapes (2x4, 4x2, 1x8) to validate topology-aware decisions.
Fault injection: simulate GPU OOM on a pipeline stage to verify eviction/replication and spill behavior.
Regression suite: compare to baseline (current slab stripe) across throughput, p50/p95 latency, and memory efficiency.
Customer-like workload replay: replay production traces for a mid-market customer to validate real-world tail behavior.
SLO validation: automated check that p95 token latency does not regress by >5% and throughput loss <3% in canary.
Telemetry sanity: validate per-cell metrics are exported and dashboards render correctly.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged behind runtime config. Start with internal canary on staging clusters with synthetic load for 48h.
Canary in our dedicated fleet (small subset of tenants) for 7 days; monitor p95 token latency, cross-GPU fetch rate, and NCCL stalls.
Gradual ramp to 25% of traffic with automatic rollback triggers tied to SLO breaches.
Open beta for private deployment customers who opt-in; collect profiling snapshots and perf traces.
Full rollout after 4 weeks and two successful canary cycles and a retro showing no regression.
Backstop controls: runtime disable and hot-reload config to change micro-slab size or disable replication if needed.
Post-release: add tuning recipes for common topologies in our docs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests pass in CI and canary clusters.
p95 token latency does not regress by more than 5% vs baseline on mixed workloads.
Cross-GPU KV fetch rate reduced by at least 30% on bursty prefix workloads in internal perf tests.
Memory utilization variance across pipeline stages reduced (standard deviation) by at least 25% in targeted topologies.
Telemetry for microgrid cells available and shows hit-rate and contention counters in dashboards.
Documentation and runtime flags added to Confluence and runtime-1.22 release notes.
No critical security findings in basic checklist and QA sign-off.
Performance regression alerting configured for canary and production.
